subject: kimi-code
title: minidb (WAL store backing engine+server persistence) excluded from every CI run: root vitest omits it and no workflow runs its suite
evidence: vitest.config.ts:8 ('!packages/minidb' in projects); grep minidb .github/workflows/*.yml -> zero hits; 33 test files incl. test/wal.test.ts:53-90 (group-commit durability) and compaction-fault.test.ts never gated
one_why: The mechanism itself verified real (wal.ts group commit, everysec fsync policy, fault injection), but a store with zero CI gating means every durability claim about it is a snapshot claim; one pnpm --filter job in ci.yml converts 33 real test files into enforcement.

subject: kimi-code
title: Phantom CI job survives the v1-engine removal: test-vscode-legacy sets KIMI_CODE_LEGACY_FLAG=1 that no code reads
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:72-88 (job + env flag); grep -r KIMI_CODE_LEGACY over apps/ and packages/ -> zero source hits; CHANGELOG confirms v1 was the default until PR #2627 and acp dropped the flag in #3434
one_why: Boundary finding against the provisional architecture docking: the dual-engine migration is COMPLETE at HEAD (no agent-core v1 package exists in the tree), so the live dual-tree penalty that anchors at 8 (cline) does not apply to kimi; what remains is dead CI scaffolding plus kimi-cli data migration, which reads as a completed-migration residue, not a second engine.

subject: kimi-code
title: Hand-written pure-TS bash parser gated by byte-for-byte differential tests against the official tree-sitter-bash 0.25.0 wasm reference, with a known-diff registry that fails loudly when a deviation is silently fixed
evidence: packages/tree-sitter-bash/test/differential.test.ts:3-16 (@known-diff samples must still differ AND match stored dump; cross-checked vs README), devDependency tree-sitter-bash@0.25.0 (package.json:44); runs in blocking CI via ci.yml:36,49
one_why: This is what makes the AST-parsed permission policy trustworthy: a from-scratch parser claiming tree-sitter parity usually rots silently into policy bypasses; pinning the reference implementation as a test oracle plus a one-way known-differences ledger means every behavioral drift in the security-relevant parser fails PR CI - copyable discipline for any hand-rolled grammar standing behind a safety claim.

subject: kimi-code
title: Unanalyzable bash fails CLOSED to ask in default mode, and the policy parses through nested wrappers (bash -c, eval, env, busybox, sudo -u) up to depth 4
evidence: packages/agent-core-v2/src/agent/permissionPolicy/policies/dangerous-command-ask.ts:145 (unanalyzable => ask, bypass only in explicit yolo/auto), :100-146; table tests permissionPolicyService.test.ts:280-303 (bash -c 'eval "shutdown now"' => ask; env -i FOO=bar shutdown => ask; rm -rf /tmp/* approved)
one_why: The corpus pattern is regex denylists that fail open on anything they cannot pattern-match; kimi's parse-abort/error path routes to ask instead of allow, and wrapper unwrapping is recursive with a bounded depth - the fail-closed-on-unknown half of an AST policy is the half most implementations quietly omit.

subject: kimi-code
title: Vendored pi-tui ruled a library dependency, not lineage: documented pin, MIT, intent cards, own CI job; no pi god-file pattern inherited
evidence: packages/pi-tui/UPSTREAM.md:10-16 (pin earendil-works/pi@53816d7..., subtree packages/tui, 2026-09-14); vendored max file src/components/editor.ts 2625 LOC vs pi's own 6852/4023 product files which are NOT vendored; .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-67 (dedicated test-pi-tui job)
one_why: Boundary ruling requested before docking: kimi-code is not a pi derivative (rule (a) N/A) - only a TUI library subtree is carried under written sync governance - and the ERRATA god-file question resolves negative: both >5k product surfaces flagged in the errata are pi-authored files absent from this tree, while kimi's large files (kimi-tui.ts 4238, sdk-rpc-client-v2.ts 2889) are own-authored with the former still under the 5k threshold.
